item.text: I’ll use the built-in `image_gen` tool only for generation, then I’ll handle the PNG bytes locally for placement and receipt hashing. No API key, curl, or repo image scripts.
The generated image is a 4:3 contact sheet. I’m locating the tool’s emitted PNG on disk now so I can copy the exact bytes to the requested artifact path and compute the receipt.
The usual temporary locations did not contain the new PNG, so I’m checking Codex’s generated image cache next. After that I’ll copy the newest generated PNG and verify the target files.
I found the new generated PNG in the Codex image cache. I’m copying that file unchanged to the requested output path, then I’ll compute dimensions and SHA-256 from the copied PNG.

dst='/mnt/storage12tb/skills/persona-dream/outputs/embry-kai-surf-phase04-contact-sheets-20260702/artifacts/images/contact_sheet_lava_reef.png'
receipt='/mnt/storage12tb/skills/persona-dream/outputs/embry-kai-surf-phase04-contact-sheets-20260702/artifacts/images/contact_sheet_lava_reef_receipt.json'
mkdir -p \""'$(dirname "$dst")"
cp "$src" "$dst"
read width height < <(identify -format '"'%w %h' \""'$dst")
sha=$(sha256sum "$dst" | awk '"'{print "'$1}'"')
printf '{\\n  \"ok\": true,\\n  \"auth\": \"codex_oauth_image_gen\",\\n  \"path\": \"%s\",\\n  \"width\": %s,\\n  \"height\": %s,\\n  \"sha256\": \"%s\"\\n}\\n' \""'$dst" "$width" "$height" "$sha" > "$receipt"
ls -l "$dst" "$receipt"
printf '"'dimensions=%sx%s\\nsha256=%s\\n' \""'$width" "$height" "$sha'
